title: Perfect tenses & sequence
subtitle: What had already happened
objectives: Form present and past perfect tenses.
Locate an earlier event relative to a past reference point.
Distinguish participles with haber from agreeing adjectives.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c3-u01. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Two reference points
lectures.body: He terminado connects completion to the present frame; había terminado places completion before another past reference point. Past perfect uses imperfect haber: había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían plus a participle. Cuando llegué, ya habían salido says their departure preceded my arrival. The past perfect is not required for every event that happened long ago; it expresses a relationship to another past moment. Ya and todavía no clarify whether the earlier event had happened by that point. Establish the reference point before choosing the compound tense.

lectures.title: Keep the compound together
lectures.body: After haber the participle stays invariant: Ellas habían escrito las cartas. Do not change it to escritas because the writers or letters are feminine. Adjectival/passive uses do agree: Las cartas estaban escritas. Common irregular participles include visto, hecho, dicho, escrito, vuelto, puesto, roto, abierto and muerto. Object pronouns precede the conjugated auxiliary: Se lo había explicado. Avoid placing them between haber and the participle. In conversation, you can unpack a confusing sequence with primero and después before restating it with the past perfect; grammar should make the relationship clearer, not more opaque.

reading: Cuando Nora llegó a la oficina, el equipo ya había empezado la reunión. Ella había enviado el informe la noche anterior, pero nadie lo había abierto: el archivo tenía un nombre poco claro. Durante la pausa, Nora explicó dónde estaba y se lo mostró a una colega. Después de la reunión escribió un mensaje: «He cambiado el nombre del archivo y he añadido una fecha. Antes no había pensado en cómo lo iban a buscar». La colega respondió que el contenido estaba bien organizado, pero que faltaba una síntesis inicial. Distingue los cambios realizados antes de la reunión, los realizados después y las reflexiones conectadas con el presente del mensaje.

worked.reason: The departure precedes another past event; plural habían agrees with ellos.
The participle stays invariant after haber; escritas would be adjectival agreement.
After estar as a resulting-state adjective, the form agrees with feminine plural cartas.
A completed event before the past call uses the past perfect auxiliary había.
Decir has the irregular participle dicho.
Abrir uses the irregular participle abierto; no plural ending is added after haber.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: They had already left.
quiz.explanation: “Ya habían salido” expresses “They had already left”. “Hasta ese momento” instead means “Up to that moment”. “Ya lo habían puesto aquí” instead means “They had already put it here”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: They had written the letters.
quiz.explanation: “Habían escrito las cartas” expresses “They had written the letters”. “Después de haberlo leído” instead means “After having read it”. “He cambiado el nombre” instead means “I have changed the name”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: The letters were written as a resulting state.
quiz.explanation: “Las cartas estaban escritas” expresses “The letters were written as a resulting state”. “No lo había pensado” instead means “I had not thought about it”. “Habíamos vuelto temprano” instead means “We had returned early”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I had finished when you called.
quiz.explanation: “Había terminado cuando llamaste” expresses “I had finished when you called”. “¿Lo habías visto antes?” instead means “Had you seen it before?”. “Ya habían salido” instead means “They had already left”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I had told it to him/her/them.
quiz.explanation: “Se lo había dicho” expresses “I had told it to him/her/them”. “Habían escrito las cartas” instead means “They had written the letters”. “Ya lo habían puesto aquí” instead means “They had already put it here”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Se lo había dicho","Todavía no había llegado","Hasta ese momento"]
quiz.explanation: “Se lo había dicho” means “I had told it to him/her/them”. “Todavía no había llegado” means “She or he had not arrived yet”. “Hasta ese momento” means “Up to that moment”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

pairs.left: I had told it to him/her/them
She or he had not arrived yet

homework.prompt: Read the original text for this unit. Identify its situation, central message, and three supporting details. Then write a new version of 150–200 words for a different person or audience. Use the target patterns, change at least three facts, and explain two revisions.
homework.model:

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Explain a project handoff using two timelines: what had been completed before a meeting and what has changed since. Have a partner reconstruct the order.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Ya habían salido / Habían escrito las cartas. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Explain a project handoff using two timelines: what had been completed before a meeting and what has changed since. Have a partner reconstruct the order.
culture: Recent-past preferences vary regionally, but the earlier-than-a-past-reference relationship of the past perfect is broadly useful. Do not replace regional present-perfect patterns with a claim that one region is less precise.
selfAssessment: I can form present and past perfect tenses.
I can locate an earlier event relative to a past reference point.
I can distinguish participles with haber from agreeing adjectives.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
